problem: The lazy-loading placeholder gate removed the original touched image when dragging began. Later touch events targeting that detached node could no longer reach document/body listeners, leaving the touch backend in a dragging state.

fix.retainedTouchTarget: Face-up card image elements stay mounted with the same src while the drag placeholder is active.
fix.placeholderStyle: Opacity zero hides the original face without removing its DOM node or layout.

regression.method: Node/jsdom simulation with the actual Angular card template, image directive and installed TouchBackend. Synthetic touch events retain the original touched IMG; hit testing is controlled. No browser automation or physical device gesture is represented by this test.

publicBrowser.method: CUA normal desktop page-load/DOM/screenshot smoke check only; no drag gesture performed.

verification.execution: Runtime, card and frontend phases passed in the npm test run. A test-only Angular UMD/Ivy bootstrap issue in the new DOM harness was fixed; touch, finalizer and packaging/cache phases were then rerun successfully.
